subject: Portable final-pass quality enforcement across code, templates, skills, prompts, scripts, documentation, pages, and…

evals.prompt: Define best-practice in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the best-practice skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind best-practice. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "reviewing PR feedback phrasing and comment classification (use code-review)". Should best-practice activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force best-practice onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to skill-scaffold, color-system-design, typography-system, test-coverage-strategy, performance-engineering, performance-budgets, visual-design-foundations, layout-composition.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "reviewing a pull request for correctness, security, and style". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying best-practice.

Place best-practice among its adjacent skills (skill-scaffold, color-system-design, typography-system, test-coverage-strategy, performance-engineering, performance-budgets, visual-design-foundations, layout-composition). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about best-practice and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
